# Agent Instructions

## Project shape

- This is a React 18 TypeScript frontend using Material UI, React Query, Valtio, and `react-scripts`.
- Application startup is in `src/index.tsx`; the root application and shared theme/configuration live in `src/`.
- Feature modules are organized under `src/features/`, with common state, validation, and hooks under `src/commons/` and `src/hooks/`.
- Treat `src/` as the source of truth. `build/` is compiled production output and should not be edited by hand.

## AI attribution

- Whenever creating a new file from scratch, add a top-of-file comment stating that the file was AI-generated by the model performing the work, naming that model.
- Whenever generative AI materially contributes to an existing file, add a brief top-of-file comment naming the model and describing in general terms what it generated or changed. The notice should indicate the approximate extent of the AI contribution without unnecessary detail.
- If the file format does not support comments, use its valid metadata mechanism when one exists; never make the file invalid just to add the notice.

## Commands

- `npm start` starts the development server.
- `npm run build` creates the production build in `build/`.
- `npm test` runs the test suite.
- `npm run lint` runs ESLint across TypeScript and TSX source files.

Run the narrowest relevant check after a change, then run `npm run build` for TypeScript or React changes. Do not treat generated build output as a source edit.

## Code conventions

- Follow the existing ESLint style: double quotes, no semicolons, curly braces, and the existing component/function naming conventions.
- Keep TypeScript strictness intact and preserve the existing public component and hook APIs unless the task requires changing them.
- Prefer existing Material UI components, theme values, state utilities, and hooks over duplicating functionality.
- Keep feature-specific UI and behavior in its existing feature directory; keep shared state, validation, and reusable hooks in their existing common directories.

## Local setup

- Runtime configuration is handled by the existing environment configuration files; do not commit secrets.
- The Twitch and YouTube integrations depend on the configured backend/API endpoints and browser third-party player APIs.
- See [`README.md`](README.md) for the project overview and local development instructions.
